approachQuestion.prompt:
Layout Packet. Convert a binary tree to a token array as follows: write its node label, then the entire left subtree packet, then the entire right subtree packet. Write # for an absent subtree. Return the packet, including the one-token packet [#] for an empty tree. The input supplies n and a writable final array of length 2n+1.

In examples, x(left,right) denotes a node labelled x, and - denotes an absent child. Example 1: Input: 5(2(-,-),8(-,-)). Output: [5,2,#,#,8,#,#]. Example 2: Input: 4(-,6(-,-)). Output: [4,#,6,#,#]. Example 3: Input: -. Output: [#].

Constraints: 0 <= n <= 200000; labels are signed 32-bit integers and may repeat; # is a distinct token. The immutable tree has child pointers only, no cycles or shared nodes. Shape is unrestricted. Use the output array only for final tokens; its unwritten slots are not scratch space.

options.text: Use a depth-first stack initially containing the root pointer, including null. Pop a pointer; emit # for null, otherwise emit its label and push its right pointer then left pointer, including nulls.
options.feedback: The reversed push order completes each left packet before the right packet. Explicit null tokens preserve every missing-child position.

options.text: At each non-null node recursively construct separate child packets and concatenate copies into a new whole-subtree packet. Finally copy the root packet into the supplied array.
options.feedback: The packet is exact for every tree, but ancestors recopy complete child packets. Direct emission avoids these intermediate copies.

options.text: Emit only node labels in root-left-right order, omitting all # tokens.
options.feedback: The output is incomplete and loses shape: 1(2(-,-),-) and 1(-,2(-,-)) would both become [1,2].

options.text: Use a FIFO queue to emit a label or # for each pointer, enqueuing non-null nodes’ left and right child pointers.
options.feedback: This encodes level order rather than subtree packets. For 1(2(3(-,-),-),4(-,-)), token 3 must come before token 4, while the queue puts 4 first.

feedback.reason: Null markers preserve shape in a root-first encoding; node labels alone do not.
details: Push the root pointer even if null. Pop a pointer: emit # and schedule nothing if null; otherwise emit its label, push its right pointer, then push its left pointer. Keep consuming the stack until empty. Write each token directly to the next slot of the supplied final array.

Emit null markers as well as real nodes; otherwise different shapes can have the same preorder labels. Push right before left so left is processed next by the stack. An empty root still emits one null token.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the revealed pointer-stack encoder consider n>=1 nodes and height h in nodes. Choose the tight worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Count the stack, including null entries, and index; exclude the tree and supplied final 2n+1-token output buffer. Each token write is constant-time; no encodings are copied.
constraints: All legal shapes are allowed; do not assume balance. Heights count nodes, not edges.

Pointer access, comparisons, arithmetic on the stated integer ranges, and allocation/release of a fixed-size frame take constant time. No hashing is used. Count all live explicit frames; the method does not use language recursion or copy paths/subtrees unless explicitly stated.

feedback.reason: Emit 2n+1 tokens while retaining only depth-first pending pointers.
details: Each real node and each missing-child token is emitted once, for 2n+1 tokens. Pending siblings and null pointers along one depth-first path use O(h) entries; a branching or left-skewed shape attains this scale.
After a node label, the stack arranges that its entire left subtree is emitted before its right subtree. A null emits exactly its marker. Induction on subtrees yields precisely the specified packet.

“O(n) time, O(h) auxiliary space”: Each real node and each missing-child token is emitted once, for 2n+1 tokens. Pending siblings and null pointers along one depth-first path use O(h) entries; a branching or left-skewed shape attains this scale.
“O(n²) time, O(h) auxiliary space”: Completed subtrees are not scanned again; nesting the control flow does not itself multiply the node visits.
“O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The live explicit stack is auxiliary memory and can grow with tree height.
“O(n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: This is a looser upper bound since h <= n; the height-sensitive bound is tighter and no full node table is retained.

methodReveal.title: Emit root then complete subtrees
methodReveal.description: Push the root pointer even if null. Pop a pointer: emit # and schedule nothing if null; otherwise emit its label, push its right pointer, then push its left pointer. Keep consuming the stack until empty. Write each token directly to the next slot of the supplied final array.
